threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a night out means a pub crawl, not a marathon of house parties. Good luck keeping up with the vibe!
Caught a glimpse of a couple on the N133 arguing about the best jerk chicken spot. Their passion had the whole back seat nodding in agreement.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I lived here was when I saw a street artist painting over a truck, while kids played football nearby. Pure Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous street art festivals where local artists throw their pieces up overnight, transforming walls before dawn.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their indifference to the BART delays—just another Tuesday. Tourists panic; we just grab a burrito and wait it out.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a dog in a backpack on the 14, totally chill. The owner just smiled at the shocked stares. Classic SF—pets and people riding together like it’s normal.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists don’t realize that the best time to enjoy the Parc Güell is at dawn. The colors and quiet give it a totally different vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the bakery—looking at the options but still ordering a plain baguette instead of a ‘barra’.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You ask the barista for soy milk and they look at you like you just landed from Mars. Whole milk is still king here.
Saw a guy on the 188 last night trying to barter with the driver for a free ride—offered a half-eaten sandwich. Driver just shook his head.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh currywurst wafting from the corner kiosk, mixed with the sound of kids playing football in the park—how could you not feel at home?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a late-night döner and hear live vinyl spinning at an underground bar, all while dodging spontaneous street art. It's magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they know to keep a few bucks handy for BART delays; the train's late, but they still saunter on, unfazed.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Spotted a guy on the 31 yelling at the driver for not stopping at a rare empty bus stop—only in SF do we complain about too few stops.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think all the locals are sipping vermut on every corner, but most of us are juggling work and life, just passing the bars on our way home.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they shoot photos of every menu item—like they're collecting souvenirs rather than enjoying the food.
